p.src: The story tells how Gongsun Sheng presented Song Jiang and Wu Yong with a plan for the formation. “It follows the method used at the end of the Han, when Zhuge Kongming arranged stones into a battle formation: sixty-four companies, eight by eight, face every direction, with the commanding general stationed at the center. Its shape has four heads and eight tails; it wheels left and turns right according to the workings of heaven, earth, wind, and cloud and the forms of dragon, tiger, bird, and serpent. When they charge down the mountain and enter the formation, our two wings will open together as though waiting to admit them. As soon as the Seven Stars signal pennant is raised, transform the formation into the shape of a long serpent. I shall then invoke my Daoist arts, leaving the three men no road ahead or behind and no gate to either side. Dig a concealed pit in the northern sector and drive all three men straight toward it. On both sides conceal men armed with hooked poles, ready to capture them.” Song Jiang was delighted by what he heard. He immediately issued his commands and ordered every officer, high and low, to carry them out. Eight fierce generals were assigned to guard the formation: Huyan Zhuo, Zhu Tong, Hua Rong, Xu Ning, Mu Hong, Sun Li, Shi Jin, and Huang Xin. Chai Jin, Lü Fang, and Guo Sheng were ordered to take temporary command of the central army; Song Jiang, Wu Yong, and Gongsun Sheng took Chen Da with them to wave the signal flags. Zhu Wu was told to lead five soldiers to a high slope near the mountain, from which they were to watch the opposing formation and report developments.

p.src: Fan Rui, the “Demon King Who Throws the World into Chaos,” rode a black horse and took his place before the formation. Xiang Chong stood at his senior side and Li Gun at his junior side. Although Fan Rui knew divine arts and sorcery, he understood nothing of battle formations. Seeing Song Jiang’s troops drawn up in formation on every side, he rejoiced inwardly. “If you form ranks like that,” he thought, “you have fallen into my trap!” He instructed Xiang Chong and Li Gun, “When you see the wind rise, lead five hundred rolling-blade fighters into their formation.” Xiang Chong and Li Gun received the order. Each gripped his barbarian shield and readied his javelins and flying swords, waiting only for Fan Rui to work his magic. Fan Rui sat upright on his horse, holding his bronze meteor hammer in his left hand and the Demon King’s treasured sword in his right. He muttered an incantation and cried, “Hasten!” At once a gale rose on every side, whipping up sand and stones until heaven and earth grew dark and neither sun nor moon gave light. Xiang Chong and Li Gun raised a battle cry and charged forward with their five hundred rolling-blade fighters. When Song Jiang’s troops saw them charging over, they parted into two wings. No sooner had Xiang Chong and Li Gun plunged into the formation than powerful bows and hard-drawn crossbows on both sides held the oncoming men at bay. Only forty or fifty followed the pair inside; all the rest retreated to their own formation. From the high slope Song Jiang saw that Xiang Chong and Li Gun had entered the formation. He ordered Chen Da to wave the Seven Stars signal flag once, and the great formation churned and rolled until it changed into the Long Serpent Formation. Within the formation, Xiang Chong and Li Gun dashed east and rushed west, wheeling left and turning right, but could find no way out. On the high slope, Zhu Wu used a small flag to direct them. When the two headed east, Zhu Wu pointed east; when they headed west, he pointed west. Gongsun Sheng, watching from a high rise, had already drawn his ancient pine-grained, block-pommel sword. He recited an incantation and cried, “Hasten!” He made the wind swirl wildly at the very heels of Xiang Chong and Li Gun. The two men saw heaven and earth grow dark within the formation and the sun lose its light. Not a single soldier or horse could be seen on any side; wherever they looked, there was only black vapor. All those who had followed behind them had vanished. Xiang Chong and Li Gun began to panic. They wanted only to force a way back to their own lines, but no matter what they tried, they could find no road of return. As they hurried along, an earth-shaking thunderclap suddenly boomed. The two cried out helplessly within the formation, lost their footing together, somersaulted, and tumbled into a concealed horse pit. Men armed with hooked poles were waiting on both sides. They promptly hauled the pair up, bound them with hempen ropes, and escorted them to the hill to claim their reward. Song Jiang pointed with the tip of his whip, and the whole army swept forward to attack. Fan Rui led his men in flight up the mountain, but more than half of those who could not escape quickly enough were lost.

p.src: Song Jiang recalled his troops, and all the chieftains took their seats before the command tent. The soldiers soon brought Xiang Chong and Li Gun before the commander’s standard. When Song Jiang saw them, he hurriedly ordered their bonds removed and personally offered them cups of wine. “You two valiant gentlemen must not take offense,” he said. “In the face of an enemy, I had no choice but to act as I did. I am Song Jiang. Long have I heard of the great names of you three valiant men, and I wished to invite you courteously to the mountain so that we might unite in the cause of righteousness. But I could find no suitable opportunity, and so the matter was delayed. If you do not disdain us and will return with us to our stronghold, nothing could bring me greater good fortune.” Hearing this, the two prostrated themselves and said, “We had already heard the great name of the ‘Timely Rain,’ but we younger brothers lacked the good fortune to meet and pay our respects to you. Now we see that you truly possess the highest righteousness, elder brother! The two of us failed to recognize a good man and sought to defy heaven and earth. Today we were captured, and even ten thousand deaths would have been a light punishment, yet you have treated us with courtesy instead. If you spare our lives, we swear to serve you unto death and repay this great kindness! What can Fan Rui accomplish without the two of us? If you righteous chieftains will release one of us to return, he will tell Fan Rui to come and submit himself. What is your honored opinion, Chief?” Song Jiang replied, “Valiant gentlemen, there is no need to keep one of you here as a hostage. I invite you both to return to your honored stronghold. Tomorrow, Song Jiang shall await your good news.” The two bowed their thanks and said, “You are truly a great man! If Fan Rui refuses to submit, we shall seize him and present him before you, Chief.” Song Jiang was overjoyed to hear this. He invited them into the central command tent, entertained them with food and wine, gave them two new suits of clothing and two fine horses, and ordered some young followers to carry their spears and shields and escort them down the mountain on their return to the stronghold.

p.src: As the two rode along, they could not thank him enough. When they reached the foot of Mount Mangdang, the young bandits were greatly astonished to see them and escorted them up to the stronghold. Fan Rui asked why they had returned. Xiang Chong and Li Gun said, “We have defied Heaven and deserve ten thousand deaths!” Fan Rui said, “Brothers, why do you say that?” The two then told him the whole story of Song Jiang’s chivalrous generosity. Fan Rui said, “Since Song Gongming is so worthy and prizes honor above all, we must not defy Heaven. Tomorrow morning we shall all descend the mountain and submit to him.” The two said, “That is precisely why we came.” That night they put the stronghold in order. At daybreak the next morning, all three descended the mountain, went straight to Song Jiang’s camp, and prostrated themselves before it. Song Jiang helped the three men up and invited them into his tent, where they took their seats. Finding not the slightest suspicion in Song Jiang, the three opened their hearts to him, and each side related the events of their lives. The three respectfully invited all the chieftains to the Mount Mangdang stronghold, where they slaughtered oxen and horses to entertain Song Gongming and the other leaders, while rewarding the troops. When the feast was over, Fan Rui formally took Gongsun Sheng as his master. Song Jiang ordered Gongsun Sheng to transmit the orthodox Heavenly Heart art of the Five Thunderbolts to Fan Rui, who was overjoyed. Within a few days they gathered the oxen and horses, packed up the stronghold’s money and provisions, loaded their baggage, assembled the men, burned the stockade, and followed Song Jiang and the others back in triumph to Liangshan Marsh. Nothing further happened on the road.

p.src: Seeing that Duan Jingzhu was no ordinary-looking man, Song Jiang was secretly delighted and said, “Since that is how matters stand, come with us to the stronghold and we shall discuss it there.” Taking Duan Jingzhu with them, they all boarded boats and went ashore at Golden Sands Beach. Heavenly King Chao and the other chieftains received them in the Hall of Righteous Assembly, where Song Jiang introduced Fan Rui, Xiang Chong, and Li Gun to all the leaders. Duan Jingzhu also paid his respects along with them. They beat the hall drum and held a celebratory feast. Seeing that the stronghold was continually gaining men and troops as heroes from every quarter flocked to its fame, Song Jiang ordered Li Yun and Tao Zongwang to oversee the construction of additional dwellings and stockades on all sides. When Duan Jingzhu again described the horse’s fine qualities, Song Jiang sent Dai Zong, the “Magic Traveler,” to Zengtou Market to learn what had become of it.

p.src: Dai Zong returned after four or five days and told the chieftains, “Zengtou Market has more than three thousand households, among them an estate called the Zeng Family Manor. The old master of that household originally came from the Great Jin realm and is known as Elder Zeng. He has five sons, known as the Five Tigers of the Zeng family: the eldest is Zeng Tu, the second Zeng Mi, the third Zeng Suo, the fourth Zeng Kui, and the fifth Zeng Sheng. They also have an instructor named Shi Wengong and a deputy instructor named Su Ding. At Zengtou Market they have gathered five to seven thousand men and horses, erected a fortified camp, and built more than fifty trap-carts. They have sworn themselves our mortal enemies, declaring that they will capture every chieftain in our stronghold. That thousand-li Jade Lion horse is now ridden by Instructor Shi Wengong. There is something still more hateful about those scoundrels: they have invented some verses and taught all the children in the market to sing, ‘Shake the iron-ring bells, and gods and demons quake in fear. Iron carts and iron chains, studded above and below with spikes. Sweep clean Liangshan’s limpid marsh; destroy Chao Gai and march him to the Eastern Capital! Take the “Timely Rain” alive, and capture the “Resourceful Star” living! The Zeng family has five tigers, whose fame is known beneath all Heaven!’” When Chao Gai heard this, he flew into a rage and cried, “How dare these beasts be so insolent! I must go there myself. I swear I shall not return to the mountain until I have captured them!” Song Jiang said, “Elder brother, you are the master of the stronghold and must not move lightly. I am willing to go.” Chao Gai said, “I am not trying to steal your merit. You have descended the mountain many times and are wearied from fighting. This time I shall go in your place. When next there is trouble, worthy brother, you shall go.” Song Jiang pleaded bitterly, but Chao Gai would not listen. In his fury, Chao Gai called up five thousand men and asked twenty chieftains to assist him in descending the mountain. All the others remained with Song Gongming to defend the stronghold.

It would be better to wait awhile before going to settle matters with those scoundrels.” Chao Gai said, “What is strange about the winds and clouds of Heaven and Earth? If we do not seize them now while the spring weather is warm, but wait until their strength has grown before advancing, it will be too late. Do not hinder me. Come what may, I am determined to go!” Song Jiang could not dissuade him. Chao Gai led his army across the water and departed. Song Jiang remained deeply dejected; after returning to the stronghold, he again sent Dai Zong down the mountain to gather news.

p.src: While Chao Gai and the other leaders were observing the place, a body of troops suddenly burst from the willow grove, some seven or eight hundred strong. At their head rode a hero in a burnished bronze helmet and linked armor, wielding a tempered-steel spear and mounted on a charger trained to break battle lines. It was Zeng Kui, the fourth son of the Zeng family. He shouted, “You rebels against the state, you bandits of Liangshan Marsh! I was just coming to seize you, deliver you to the authorities, and claim my reward. Heaven itself has granted me this opportunity! Why do you not dismount and submit to bonds? What are you waiting for?” Chao Gai flew into a rage. Glancing back, he saw that one of his commanders had already ridden out to engage Zeng Kui. It was Panther Head Lin Chong, one of the heroes who had joined Liangshan in its earliest days. The two crossed horses and fought for more than twenty bouts, with neither gaining the advantage. After twenty bouts, Zeng Kui realized that he could not overcome Lin Chong. He drew back his spear, wheeled his horse, and fled toward the willow grove. Lin Chong reined in and did not pursue. Chao Gai led his troops back to camp, where they discussed how to attack Zengtou Market. Lin Chong said, “Tomorrow we should go straight to the entrance of the market and challenge them. Once we have seen the true state of their defenses, we can deliberate further.” At daybreak the next morning, they led five thousand troops to the level, open ground before Zengtou Market, drew up their battle formation, beat the drums, and raised a great shout. At the boom of a cannon from Zengtou Market, a great body of troops emerged. Seven heroes stood arrayed in a single line: in the center was the chief instructor Shi Wengong; above him, the deputy instructor Su Ding; below him, the eldest Zeng son, Zeng Tu; to the left were Zeng Mi and Zeng Kui; and to the right, Zeng Sheng and Zeng Suo. All were fully armed and armored. Instructor Shi Wengong carried a bow with arrows at his side, rode a thousand-li Jade Lion horse, and wielded a painted halberd of the Square Heaven pattern. After the drums had sounded three times, several prison carts were pushed from the Zeng formation and placed before the lines. Zeng Tu pointed at the opposing army and cursed, “You rebels against the state, you thieving rabble! Do you see our prison carts? If we merely killed you at the Zeng manor, we would not count as heroes! We mean to take every one of you alive, load you into these prison carts, escort you to the Eastern Capital, and cut your bodies into ten thousand pieces. Surrender while there is still time, and there may yet be something to discuss.” Hearing this, Chao Gai was enraged. Leveling his spear, he rode straight at Zeng Tu. Fearing that harm might befall Chao Gai, all his commanders charged forward together, and the two armies became locked in a confused melee. The Zeng troops retreated step by step into the village. Lin Chong and Huyan Zhuo kept close guard around Chao Gai as they pursued and slew the enemy to east and west. Seeing that the roads were treacherous, Lin Chong hurried back and called off the troops. It appeared that both sides had lost some men and horses. Chao Gai returned to the camp. His heart was deeply troubled. The commanders consoled him, saying, “Elder Brother, set your mind at ease. Do not grieve and brood, lest you harm your honored health. In the past, when Elder Brother Song Gongming led troops to war, he too suffered setbacks, yet in the end he won and returned to camp. In today’s melee, each side lost some men and horses, but we were not defeated by them. Why should you grieve?” Yet Chao Gai remained gloomy and joyless. For three days in succession they remained in camp and issued a challenge each day, but not a single person appeared from Zengtou Market.

p.src: On the fourth day, two monks suddenly came straight to Chao Gai’s camp and sought an audience. The soldiers led them before the central command tent. The two monks knelt and reported, “We humble monks are the stewards of Fahua Temple, east of Zengtou Market. The Five Tigers of the Zeng family constantly come to our temple and torment us, demanding gold, silver, money, and valuables, and committing every kind of outrage. We know all the details of their defenses and movements, and have come expressly to beg you leaders to enter and raid their stockade. If you destroy them, our whole district will be blessed.” Chao Gai was delighted by their words. He invited the two monks to sit and had wine set out for them. Lin Chong cautioned him, “Elder Brother, do not readily believe them. Might there not be some trick in this?” One monk said, “We humble monks are men who have left the world. How would we dare speak falsely? We have long heard that Liangshan Marsh follows the way of benevolence and righteousness and never harasses the people wherever its forces pass. That is why we came especially to offer our services. Why would we deliberately come to lure you generals into a trap? Besides, the Zeng family may not even be able to defeat your great army. Why should you suspect us?” Chao Gai said, “Brother, do not let suspicion arise and spoil this great undertaking. Tonight I shall go there myself.” Lin Chong said, “Elder Brother, do not go. Let half of us take troops to raid the stockade, while you remain outside to support us.” Chao Gai said, “If I do not go myself, who will be willing to advance? You may remain outside with half the troops to provide support.” Lin Chong asked, “Whom will you take inside with you, Elder Brother?” Chao Gai replied, “Choose ten leaders, and divide off two thousand five hundred men to go inside.” The ten leaders were Liu Tang, Ruan Xiaoer, Huyan Zhuo, Ruan Xiaowu, Ou Peng, Ruan Xiaoqi, Yan Shun, Du Qian, Song Wan, and Bai Sheng. That evening, after preparing and eating their meal, they removed the bells from the horses’ bridles and had the soldiers place gags in their mouths. They hurried through the darkness, silently following the two monks straight to Fahua Temple. When they looked, they saw an ancient monastery. Chao Gai dismounted and entered the temple. Seeing no community of monks, he asked the two, “How is it that in such a large monastery there is not a single monk?” The monks replied, “It is because those beasts of the Zeng family tormented them so cruelly that they had no choice but to return separately to secular life. Only the abbot and a few attendants remain, living in the pagoda compound. Let the leaders station the troops here for the moment. When the night is deeper, we humble monks will lead you straight into those villains’ stockade.” Chao Gai asked, “Where is their stockade?” The monks replied, “They have four stockades. The northern one is where the Zeng brothers have stationed their troops. If you can take that stockade alone, none of the others will matter. The other three stockades can be disregarded.” Chao Gai asked, “At what time can we go?” The monks replied, “It is only the second watch now. Wait until the third watch, when they will be unprepared.” At first they heard the watch drums sounding at Zengtou Market, regular and orderly; but after another half-watch had passed, not a single watch signal could be heard. The monks said, “The soldiers seem to have fallen asleep. We can go now.” The monks went ahead to lead the way. Chao Gai mounted with his commanders, led the troops out of Fahua Temple, and followed the monks.

p.src: They had gone scarcely more than five li when the two monks vanished into the darkness, and the vanguard dared go no farther. The paths all around were tangled and difficult, and not a single dwelling could be seen. The soldiers grew alarmed and reported the matter to Chao Gai. Huyan Zhuo immediately ordered them to hurry back by the way they had come. Before they had gone a hundred paces, gongs and drums sounded on every side, shouts shook the earth, and torches filled the view. Chao Gai and his commanders led their troops in a dash for an escape route. They had barely rounded two bends when a body of horsemen burst out and loosed a storm of arrows straight at them. One arrow struck Chao Gai squarely in the face and knocked him backward from his horse. Huyan Zhuo and Yan Shun spurred their horses forward in a desperate charge, while Liu Tang and Bai Sheng came up from behind, helped Chao Gai onto a horse, and fought their way out of the village. At the village entrance, Lin Chong and the others brought troops to their aid and only then managed to hold the enemy at bay. The two armies fought in confusion until daybreak, when each withdrew to its own camp. When Lin Chong returned and mustered the troops, the three Ruan brothers, Song Wan, and Du Qian had escaped with their lives through the water. Of the twenty-five hundred men who had gone in, only twelve or thirteen hundred remained; those who had followed Ou Peng also returned to the command tent. When the chieftains gathered to examine Chao Gai, they found the arrow lodged in his cheek. They hastily pulled it out, and he fainted from loss of blood. On examining the arrow, they saw the name Shi Wengong inscribed upon it. Lin Chong ordered golden-spear wound medicine to be applied, but the shaft proved to be a poisoned arrow. Stricken by the arrow's poison, Chao Gai could no longer speak. Lin Chong had him helped into a cart and sent the three Ruan brothers, Du Qian, and Song Wan to escort him back to the stronghold ahead of the rest. The remaining fifteen chieftains conferred in camp: “This time our elder brother, Heavenly King Chao, came down from the mountain only to meet with this calamity. It truly fulfilled the omen of the command flag being snapped by the wind. We can only withdraw our troops and return. Zengtou Market cannot be taken in haste.” Huyan Zhuo said, “We must wait for an order from our elder brother Song Gongming before we can withdraw.” All that day the chieftains remained sunk in gloom. The soldiers too had lost all desire to fight, and every man longed to return to the mountain.

p.src: That night, around the second watch, a faint light showed in the sky. The fifteen chieftains sat brooding in camp. As a snake cannot move without a head or a bird fly without wings, they sighed and lamented, at a loss whether to advance or retreat. Suddenly, a scout posted along the road rushed in and reported, “Four or five columns of troops are attacking from ahead, with more torches than can be counted!” At this, Lin Chong and all the others mounted their horses. Torches blazed together on the hills on three sides, lighting the scene as brightly as day, while battle cries rose on every side and swept up to the camp. Lin Chong led the chieftains away without engaging the enemy. They struck camp at once, wheeled their horses, and fled. The Zeng family's forces came sweeping after them from behind, and the two armies fought as they moved. Only after retreating fifty or sixty li did they finally shake off their pursuers. When they counted the troops, they found they had lost another five to seven hundred men. Utterly routed and defeated, they hurried back along the old road toward Liangshan Marsh. Halfway back, they met Dai Zong bringing an order that the chieftains were to lead the troops home to the stronghold for the time being and devise another sound plan. Obeying the order, the commanders led the troops back to the stronghold in the marsh. When they climbed the mountain to see Chief Chao, he could no longer swallow even water or rice, took no food at all, and was swollen all over. Song Jiang and the others kept vigil weeping at his bedside, personally applying medicines and pouring medicinal decoctions and powders down his throat. All the chieftains stood watch outside the chamber. At the third watch that night, Chao Gai's condition grew grave. Turning his head toward Song Jiang, he charged him: “Take care of yourself, worthy brother. Whoever captures the man who shot me dead—make him lord of Liangshan Marsh!” With those words, he closed his eyes and died. When Song Jiang saw that Chao Gai was dead, he grieved as though he had lost both father and mother and wept until he fainted. The chieftains supported Song Jiang as they brought him out to take charge of affairs. Wu Yong and Gongsun Sheng urged him, “Elder brother, restrain your grief. Life and death are ordained for every man; why torment yourself so bitterly? For now, please attend to the great matters before us.” When Song Jiang had finished weeping, he ordered the body washed with fragrant water, dressed in burial robes and headdress, and laid in state in the Hall of Righteous Assembly. All the chieftains came to mourn and offer sacrifices. Meanwhile, they had an inner coffin and outer case made. At an auspicious hour they placed the body solemnly in the main hall, raised a mourning canopy, and set a spirit tablet in the center inscribed: “Spirit Tablet of Lord Chao, the Heavenly King, Master of Liangshan Marsh.” Every chieftain in the stronghold, beginning with Song Gongming, wore full mourning. The lesser officers and all the rank-and-file men also wore mourning headcloths. The arrow upon which they swore vengeance was enshrined before the spirit altar. Long funeral streamers were raised throughout the stronghold, and monks from nearby temples were invited up the mountain to perform rites for the repose of Heavenly King Chao. Each day Song Jiang led the company in mourning and had no heart to manage the affairs of the stronghold. Lin Chong, Gongsun Sheng, Wu Yong, and the other chieftains conferred and resolved to establish Song Gongming as lord of Liangshan Marsh, with everyone respectfully obeying his commands.

p.src: Early the next morning, amid incense, flowers, lamps, and candles, Lin Chong took the lead and, together with the others, invited Song Gongming into the Hall of Righteous Assembly and seated him there. Wu Yong and Lin Chong began: “Elder brother, hear our petition: ‘A realm cannot go a single day without a sovereign, nor a household a single day without a master.’ Chief Chao has passed from this world; how can the enterprise of our stronghold remain without a master? Throughout the four seas all have heard your great name. Tomorrow is an auspicious day and hour; we ask you to become master of the stronghold, and all of us will respectfully obey your commands.” Song Jiang replied, “As Heavenly King Chao lay dying, he charged us: ‘Whoever captures Shi Wengong shall be made lord of Liangshan Marsh.’ Every chieftain here knows of those words. His bones are not yet cold—how could we forget them? Moreover, his enemy has not been avenged and his wrong not redressed. How could I take this seat now?” Scholar Wu urged him again: “Though Heavenly King Chao did indeed say so, that man has not yet been captured. How can the stronghold remain even one day without a master? If you will not occupy the seat, who would dare assume it? Who then is to command the men and horses of the stronghold? Despite his last words, please condescend to take this seat provisionally and occupy it for the present. We can make other arrangements when the time comes.” Song Jiang said, “The military adviser speaks most reasonably. Today I shall provisionally assume this seat. u.src: Early the next morning, amid incense, flowers, lamps, and candles, Lin Chong took the lead and, together with the others, invited Song Gongming into the Hall of Righteous Assembly and seated him there.
Wu Yong and Lin Chong began: “Elder brother, hear our petition: ‘A realm cannot go a single day without a sovereign, nor a household a single day without a master.’
Chief Chao has passed from this world; how can the enterprise of our stronghold remain without a master?

If you will not occupy the seat, who would dare assume it?

p.src: When Song Jiang had finished burning incense, he provisionally took the chief seat and sat in the foremost chair. At the head on one side sat the strategist Wu Yong, and below him Gongsun Sheng; the left-hand rank was headed by Lin Chong, and the right-hand rank by Huyan Zhuo. After all had paid their respects, they sat down in the two ranks. Song Jiang then said, “That I provisionally occupy this place today is entirely due to the support of you, my brothers. Let us be of one heart and mind, serving together as one another’s limbs and carrying out Heaven’s justice. Our stronghold now has far more men and horses than before, so I propose that the brothers be divided among six camps. The Hall of Righteous Assembly shall henceforth be renamed the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness. Four land camps shall be established to the front, rear, left, and right; two smaller camps behind the mountain; three fortified passes before the mountain; one naval camp below it; and two smaller camps on the two shoals. Today the brothers shall each be assigned their respective commands. In the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness, I provisionally occupy the place of honor; the second place goes to the strategist Scholar Wu, the third to the Daoist master Gongsun Sheng, the fourth to Hua Rong, the fifth to Qin Ming, the sixth to Lü Fang, and the seventh to Guo Sheng. In the left army camp, the first place goes to Lin Chong, the second to Liu Tang, the third to Shi Jin, the fourth to Yang Xiong, the fifth to Shi Xiu, the sixth to Du Qian, and the seventh to Song Wan. In the right army camp, the first place goes to Huyan Zhuo, the second to Zhu Tong, the third to Dai Zong, the fourth to Mu Hong, the fifth to Li Kui, the sixth to Ou Peng, and the seventh to Mu Chun. In the front army camp, the first place goes to Li Ying, the second to Xu Ning, the third to Lu Zhishen, the fourth to Wu Song, the fifth to Yang Zhi, the sixth to Ma Lin, and the seventh to Shi En. In the rear army camp, the first place goes to Chai Jin, the second to Sun Li, the third to Huang Xin, the fourth to Han Tao, the fifth to Peng Qi, the sixth to Deng Fei, and the seventh to Xue Yong. In the naval camp, the first place goes to Li Jun, the second to Ruan Xiaoer, the third to Ruan Xiaowu, the fourth to Ruan Xiaoqi, the fifth to Zhang Heng, the sixth to Zhang Shun, the seventh to Tong Wei, and the eighth to Tong Meng. The six camps shall comprise forty-three leaders in all. Lei Heng and Fan Rui are assigned to guard the first pass before the mountain. Xie Zhen and Xie Bao are assigned to guard the second pass. Xiang Chong and Li Gun are assigned to guard the third pass. The smaller camp at Golden Sands Shoal is assigned to Yan Shun, Zheng Tianshou, Kong Ming, and Kong Liang to guard. The smaller camp at Duck’s Beak Shoal is assigned to Li Zhong, Zhou Tong, Zou Yuan, and Zou Run to guard. Of the two smaller camps behind the mountain, the land camp on the left is assigned to Wang the Short Tiger, Ten Feet of Blue, and Cao Zheng. The land camp on the right is assigned to Zhu Wu, Chen Da, and Yang Chun, making six people in all, to guard. Within the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness, in the rooms along the left side, Xiao Rang shall keep the records. Pei Xuan shall administer rewards and punishments. Jin Dajian shall keep the seals and credentials. Jiang Jing shall keep accounts of money and provisions. In the rooms along the right side, Ling Zhen shall oversee the cannon. Meng Kang shall oversee shipbuilding. Hou Jian shall oversee the making of clothing and armor. Tao Zongwang shall oversee the construction of walls and ramparts. Among the officers working in the two wings behind the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness, Li Yun shall supervise building construction. Tang Long shall be superintendent of the blacksmiths. Zhu Fu shall supervise the brewing of wine and vinegar. Song Qing shall supervise preparations for banquets. Du Xing and Bai Sheng shall manage the stores and implements. At the four lookout inns on the roads below the mountain, the previously fixed assignments of Zhu Gui, Yue He, Shi Qian, Li Li, Sun Xin, Mistress Gu, Zhang Qing, and Sun Erniang shall remain unchanged. Yang Lin, Shi Yong, and Duan Jingzhu shall purchase horses in the northern regions. Now that all assignments have been made, each shall abide by them and none may disobey.” Within the outlaw stronghold at Liangshan Marsh, every leader great and small rejoiced once Song Gongming became lord of the stronghold, and all respectfully submitted to his commands. One day, Song Jiang gathered the company for consultation, intending to avenge Chao Gai by raising an army against Zengtou Market.

p.src: One day they invited a monk named Dayuan to the stronghold. He was a monk of Longhua Temple within the city of Daming Prefecture in the Northern Capital and, while traveling from place to place, had come to Jining. As he passed by Liangshan Marsh, he was invited into the stronghold to conduct a Buddhist service. While they were eating the vegetarian meal and chatting idly, Song Jiang asked about the customs and notable people of the Northern Capital. Monk Dayuan replied, “How is it that you leaders have never heard the name of Hebei’s ‘Jade Qilin’?” Hearing this, Song Jiang and Wu Yong suddenly remembered and said, “Look at us! We are not yet old, yet already so forgetful! There is indeed a wealthy gentleman in the Northern Capital named Lu Junyi, nicknamed the ‘Jade Qilin,’ who is one of the three wonders of Hebei. His family has lived in the Northern Capital for generations; he is a superb martial artist and has no equal under Heaven with staff or cudgel. If our Liangshan Marsh stronghold could obtain this man, why should we fear pursuit by government troops, or worry when their armies came against us?” Wu Yong laughed and said, “Brother, why do you dishearten yourself? If you want this man to come up the mountain, what difficulty could there be?” Song Jiang replied, “He is the foremost gentleman of Daming Prefecture in the Northern Capital. How could we possibly induce him to come here and become an outlaw?” Scholar Wu said, “I too have had him in mind for a long time, but somehow I had forgotten all about him. Let me employ one small stratagem, and I shall have the man come up the mountain himself.” Song Jiang said at once, “Men call you the ‘Resourceful Star,’ and truly your reputation is no empty one! May I ask what stratagem our strategist will use to lure the man up the mountain?” Without the least haste, Wu Yong raised two fingers together and explained the scheme. And so it came about that Lu Junyi would cast aside his brocaded luxury and jeweled splendor to brave a dragon’s pool and tiger’s den. Indeed: merely because one man joined the outlaws of the marsh, the common people were made to suffer the ravages of war. But just how Scholar Wu lured Lu Junyi up the mountain will be revealed in the next chapter.
